merged.overview:
This is the merged list from seven audits of the game at commit 5f9da45, each checked by a second reader, plus a follow-up check of eight gaps a critic found (all eight were real; one turned out wider than stated). Nothing was run or changed. The working folder is on branch ui2, at the same commit as main. In the evidence, "game/" means /Users/hunterjolly/Desktop/JJKgame.md/game, "docs/" and "tools/" sit beside it, and "shots/" means /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hunterjolly-Desktop-JJKgame-md/e3d2f368-fc62-40d2-bb70-0a23434a2d40/scratchpad.

The short version:

- The campus is in good shape. All 24 places, the six area maps and the Tokyo map are painted, and all 11 campus people have a full sprite with six faces. One caution from the follow-up: the backgrounds come in two looks, a soft dim one (the three offices, the Library) and a bright crisp one (courtyard, gate, ridge), judged from 8 of the 51 pictures.
- None of the places you asked for exists: no boys' dormitory, no teachers' lounge or quarters. At Night five people are simply "off campus" (Megumi, Toge, Yaga, Utahime, Ijichi), Yuji and Panda stand in the garden, and Nobara and Maki are behind a door that never opens, because nothing in the game ever gives the invitation.
- Everything off campus is a stand-in. Ten flat drawn pictures and eight tinted copies of them carry the whole prologue, the Sun Mall, the Nade missions, all eight board jobs and all five Tokyo districts. The first level of the campus map is also a flat drawing. Your own stand-in list in docs/PLAYTEST.md leaves most of these out.
- People stand; they do not do things, and never with each other. Of 43 person-and-place pairs in the weekly routine, 2 have a painted pose, 12 more are planned, and 21 do not even have their own caption. Four of the twelve planned poses are written for an object the picture does not show (a desk, a vending machine, the veil, a car). A painted pose disappears the moment you click the person.
- After the prologue, faces stop moving. The 25 character scenes have no face change in about 825 lines, although every person has six faces painted. This is a script pass, not art.
- 13 of the 24 places have nothing in the picture to click except exits, and the pictures are full of painted things that do nothing (the pond, the striking posts, Gojo's TV, the board-game boxes).
- Nothing teaches a new player how the place view works, and icon names show only under a mouse pointer with no setting to change that.
- The menus, save screen, choice lists and quick menu are still Ren'Py's stock screens in the game's colours. There is no sound at all.
- The card-table invite, chess, memory and tic-tac-toe are asked for and not built.
- The storyboard's new cast (18 people and creatures, Sukuna in Yuji's body first) has no sprites; that belongs mostly to the story acts but is the largest single art cost on the list.

Art already planned and priced is small (twelve poses and blink-and-talk for ten people, about $6.72). The rest of the list is new; see the art estimate. No prompt file exists for any missing background, so each needs one written before you can run anything.

groups.title: 1. New places: dormitories, the teachers' place, and where people are at Night

Because nobody else has a room, the Night column of the schedule is mostly empty, and the story already speaks of a first-year corridor that cannot be visited. The painted bird's-eye maps have spare buildings for all of this, but the pictures you stand in (the garden, the staff steps) do not show those buildings, and the Dormitories map is already at its five-pin limit. Almost every item here waits on a decision from you, so the questions matter more than the sizes.

I list them by where you meet them, biggest first. One painted picture often fixes several places at once (the morning street is also the base of two Tokyo districts). None of these has a prompt file yet. The last items are about the painted campus pictures themselves: things scenes and captions name that are not in them, and the two looks the set comes in.

Rates used (docs/ART_PHASE2.md "What things cost", and the relight tool): a background is about $0.07 (two versions at $0.035); a painted pose about $0.32 (two versions at $0.16); blink and talk about $0.32 a person ($0.16 for talk only); an icon sheet about $0.32; a relight of an approved day picture $0.16 a picture (tools/make_relight_workflow.py:26; about $0.32 if you want two versions to choose from); a foreground layer is free. A new character sprite is about $2 in edits plus the base run (docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md; the storyboard says the same). Big-moment pictures are the storyboard's guess of about $0.50 each and have never been tested.

ALREADY PLANNED IN ART_PHASE2 (about $6.72)
- 12 painted poses (24 renders): about $3.84. Caution: four of them (Yaga at a desk, Yuji at the vending machine, Gojo outside the veil, Ijichi beside the car) are written for an object the picture does not show. A pose fits only the picture it was painted on, so settle and paint the object first or those four ($1.28) may be paid for twice.
- Blink and talk for ten people (18 pictures): about $2.88.
- Optional there: Shoko at night $0.32, Sana's blink and talk $0.32.

NEW, IF YOU DID EVERYTHING ON THIS LIST (ranges depend on your answers)
- New backgrounds: about 35 for the core set, up to about 77 with everything. Core: the new places by day (3 to 6), the prologue (8: alley, diner, three home pictures, street, Nade's door, car), the ridge veil (1), a general city (1), the Sun Mall (3), the Nade sites (2), the two general curse-site pictures (2), board job sites (4 shared, or 8), the campus map (1), five districts (5), club and market (2), a title picture and a menu ground (2). On top: the storyboard's nine story places, about six other campus ideas (lake, basement, workshop and so on), fifteen district spots, and up to four yard or area-map repaints. Cost: about $2.50 for the core, about $5.40 for everything.
- Relights (evening or night versions): about 6 that people actually stand on (garden night, library evening, cafeteria evening, courtyard evening and night, ridge night), plus a night version for each new place (3 to 6), the dark alley and two district nights (3), up to 7 more outdoor nights, 7 indoor rooms and my room's evening. 12 to about 33 pictures: about $1.90 to $5.30 at one version each, double with two.
- Small edits to painted pictures: the vending machine (1), the laptop (2), the veil on the ridge (1), a car at the gate (1), a desk and photograph in Yaga's office (1), Utahime's pose redo (1): about $1.10 to $2.20.
- New painted poses beyond the planned twelve: 10 for captions that already name something ($3.20); up to 21 more if every routine cell gets one, 5 for Gojo's wandering, about 5 for second poses where a story caption disagrees, and about 5 activity pictures. 10 to about 46 poses: about $3.20 to $14.70. Group pictures for the busy hours (cafeteria at noon, Common Room evening, riverside weekend) would be about $0.32 each, each fixed to who is there.
- Faces: Sana (2 pictures, $0.32); Sukuna's cheek-mouth overlay on Yuji (1 picture, about $0.16). A talking mouth for each extra face people really use is roughly one picture per person per face ($0.16 each); not counted until you decide.
- New sprites, this overhaul's own: Mom, Dad, Kurose, Nade and Oda if she is ever seen (4 or 5, about $10 for five); curses (2 to 4); the Divine Dog and Yaga's doll (2); a market seller (1); optionally the five journal cast. At about $2 each: about $18 to $32.
- New sprites, the storyboard's cast: 18 more (Sukuna in Yuji's body first, the detention center's special grade, four ordinary curses by grade, and twelve named people), about $36 at the storyboard's rate. The four ordinary curses overlap the curses line above, so about $28 on top of it. This alone is more than the whole line before it, and it belongs mostly to the story acts.
- Outfits are a six-face set per person and are not priced in the notes; not counted.
- Icons: one new sheet covers new rooms, five yard icons and three quick-menu icons: about $0.32.

playthroughGuide: You do NOT need to write down: which backgrounds are stand-ins, which people are block figures, which places have nothing to click, who has no pose or no blink, which rooms lack a night picture, which storyboard characters have no sprite, or that there is no sound. This list has all of those, with files.

You also need not note the known layout leftovers (labels touching icons, the +1 chip, Megumi in front of the TV, the second column in the garden at night) unless one bothers you more than the notes suggest; then say how much.
What only you can tell us is how it feels. For each place, one line: did you want to stay, or did you walk straight through? What did you reach for that was not there?

Start a new game and play the first day as if you had never seen it. Nothing teaches the place view today. Where would a new player be lost: clicking the picture, finding names under the pointer, the two-click map, Hold the hour and Wait, the night rule?
Put the mouse aside for a few minutes and try the arrow keys or a controller in a place. Can you reach the things in the picture at all? Nobody could check this without running the game.
In every room, note the first painted thing you tried to click that did nothing. That order is the priority list for making things come alive.

Walk from the bright courtyard into Yaga's office, Utahime's office, Gojo's office and the Library, and back out. Does it feel like a change of light, or like a different artist? We only opened 8 of the 51 pictures for this, so your eye decides.
Night: walk the campus at Night for a few days. Does it feel empty, lonely on purpose, or broken? Where did you expect to find someone? Do Yuji and Panda in the garden look pasted on?
Go to the girls' dormitory door in the evening and at Night. Does the locked line read as a promise or a dead end?
After dark, look at the Library in the evening, the cafeteria in the evening, the courtyard and the ridge at Night. Which tinted pictures actually bother you, and which are fine?

Go to the cafeteria at noon, the Common Room on a weekday evening and the river on a weekend afternoon. Does a row of people standing apart feel like friends together? What did you expect them to be doing with each other?
Click Nobara on the sofa and Utahime at her desk. Does the jump from the painted person to the standing sprite bother you? Does Utahime read as two different people?
Talk to one person in the cafeteria at noon. Does it feel wrong that the other four vanish?
Watch Yuji talk and blink for a minute. Does the mouth look right? Does it matter that it only moves on his calm face?

Stand in a room without hovering. Can you tell what anyone is doing? Then hover: do the captions match what you see? Look in particular at the four captions that name something not painted: Yuji's vending machine, Ijichi's car, the veil on the ridge, Yaga's desk.

Play two or three character scenes and one of the top friendship scenes. Note where you wanted a face to change, someone to move, or the picture to change, and where a choice list covered a face you wanted to see.
Start a character scene from the "wrong" room (pick Yuji in the cafeteria). Does being moved to the roof and back feel odd?
Play the prologue once with fresh eyes. Which stand-in hurts most: the alley, the diner, the home rooms, the parents? That sets the order for the art.
Play the Sun Mall and one board job. Note the moments where the screen showed nothing of what the text described, and whether the switch from "I" to "you" in the telling jars.
Open the map at different hours and from different places. Is the first level (the flat drawing) confusing against the painted areas? Do you ever lose track of where you are?
Walk between areas by the exits only, no map. Where did you get lost, and which exit did you not recognise as a door or path?
Title screen, save and load, preferences: we have no screenshots of these. Note anything that looks unfinished, and whether you can tell your saves apart.
Play cards on a weekday evening and at a weekend. Who did you wish you could ask to the table? Do the buttons need explaining?
Fish a few times and read a few pages on the computer. Too fast, too slow, too plain? Did you expect pictures on the pages?
Take a day trip and a night out in Tokyo. What did you expect to be able to do there?
Anything that reads as a note to a developer rather than part of the game ("later build", "combat update"): does it bother you as a player?
Sizes: does anyone look too big or too small for the furniture, or float, in a place we have no screenshot of (dojo, gate, Yaga's office, Gojo's office, storehouse, forest, rooftop, the yards)?
Finally, one list in your own words: the five things you expected a game like this to have and did not find.
